comment: Conflict-repair Move vectors per spec authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.7 (head_in precondition + recovery_capability). When a cas-register cell sits at Bottom (Conflict), a recovery-authorised Move with `head_in [head_a, head_b]` writes a NEW value that supersedes both heads. The lattice itself doesn't peek at payload semantics — at the lattice layer, the post-recovery view is a single anchored op, which resolves to Value. Self-authorising 'winner' payloads MUST NOT be unilaterally selected by the cas-register; authorisation is enforced at verify_move (above the lattice). Manual repair is a higher-authority operator action that takes a snapshot, picks one of the conflicting values, and writes a fresh signed Move that carries `repair_of [move_id_a, move_id_b]`.

vectors.name: head_in_single_op_resolves_existing_bottom
vectors.comment: Anchor view AFTER recovery: only the repair Move is in scope (the earlier conflict pair was rolled back / superseded by the recovery anchor). cas-register sees a single anchored op ⇒ resolves to Value, clearing the prior Bottom.

expected.rationale: Single anchored Move post-recovery; cas-register resolves to Value.

vectors.name: self_authorising_winner_rejected_at_lattice_layer
vectors.comment: Two concurrent set-Moves where one self-references its own 'winner' capability remain a Bottom at the lattice layer. The cas-register doesn't peek at payload semantics; it sees concurrent writes and surfaces Bottom. Self-authorisation prevention is the AUTH layer's job (verify_move), but the lattice MUST NOT be tricked into picking a winner just because one payload claims authority.

expected.rationale: cas-register MUST NOT pick winner from self-authorising payload at the lattice layer. Bottom MUST surface both move_ids and both head values.

vectors.name: manual_repair_via_recovery_capability_holder
vectors.comment: Manual repair scenario: an operator with `cap:01js0rc0...` capability picks one of the conflicting values, writes a fresh signed Move that carries `repair_of [move_id_a, move_id_b]`, and the lattice resolves to that single Value. The recovery_capability MUST be issued by the Space's anchorer (no self-authorising loops).

expected.rationale: Recovery-capability holder unilaterally picks 'invite'; lattice surfaces Value once the prior heads are out of scope.

negative_vectors.name: repair_without_recovery_capability_rejected
negative_vectors.comment: A Move with `head_in` but NO `recovery_capability` MUST be rejected at verify_move. The lattice would happily resolve a single op to Value; the AUTH layer is the gate.

expected.rationale: head_in implies a repair Move; without recovery_capability the move is unauthorised.

negative_vectors.name: repair_head_in_does_not_match_actual_bottom_heads
negative_vectors.comment: head_in declares heads [x, y] but the cell's actual Bottom heads are [a, b]. The Move MUST be rejected (drifted repair target).

expected.rationale: The repair targets heads that aren't the cell's current Bottom heads — likely a stale operator view; reject and force re-fetch.
